title: Reliability Ops Accordion Plan: modular SLO activation and runbook rollout
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, modular plan to coordinate SLO adoption, small-runbook rollouts, and reliability experiments across product teams using an "accordion" model: compressed, iterative bursts of cross-functional work that expand and contract scope so we can learn quickly while limiting blast radius.

Context / why this differs from previous SLO drives:
- Many previous efforts tried big-bang SLO definitions or monolithic playbooks. Those created heavy upfront coordination and stalled progress.
- The accordion approach intentionally stages small, runnable units (mini-sprints) that can be folded out into broader scopes once confidence is proven.
- Goal: accelerate measurable reliability wins (latency P95 improvements, tail-failure mitigation, alert noise reduction) while keeping the number of dependent teams small during early experiments.

Scope:
- Initial scope focuses on model-serving surface and upstream routing (hosted API + Dedicated routing policies).
- Targeted services for the first three mini-sprints: inference-gateway, kv-cache-proxy, model-router-service.
- Artifacts: canonical SLO definition per service, short runbook (2 pages max), automation tasks (alert tuning, dashboards), and a small regression test harness for request-level latency.

Guiding principles:
- Small, evidence-driven changes: ship hypothesis -> measure -> iterate.
- Automate early: if a mitigation is manual more than twice in 30 days, automate it.
- Safe rollouts: default to local canary then cluster canary; global blast only with explicit sign-off.
- Share learnings: publish a 1-page retrospective after each mini-sprint.

Accordion mechanics (unique):
- Compress phase (1 week): define hypothesis, owner, minimal metric set, and quick instrumentation tasks. No more than 3 owners across teams.
- Expand phase (2–3 weeks): run targeted experiments on 1–2 services; apply routing fallbacks, cache hot-key mitigations, or batching tweaks.
- Contract phase (1 week): bake runbooks, triage open automations, decide to ship, rollback, or escalate.
- Repeat cadence: 5-week cycle per accordion iteration; multiple accordion threads can run in parallel but must register in the registry (see linked_artifacts).

Phases and sample sprint plan (first three accordion iterations):
1) Iteration A - Latency tail reduction (5 weeks)
  - Compress (wk1): owners: Ethan (platform infra), Lina (serving runtime), Product SME: Arjun. Hypothesis: intermittent P99 spikes driven by KV cache cold-starts for long prompts. Metrics: P50/P95/P99, cold-hit ratio, end-to-end latency heatmap. Preliminary tickets: JIRA-REL-1501 (instrumentation), JIRA-REL-1502 (sampling probe).
  - Expand (wk2-3): deploy prefix caching heartbeat, adjust KV prefetch policy, craft canary where 5% traffic uses new prefetch. Observe 2x reduction in cold-hit latency?
  - Contract (wk4-5): author runbook section: "KV cold-start detection and mitigation"; automate alert for cold-hit-rate > 5% for 15m; if successful, schedule rollout config gate for Dedicated clusters.
2) Iteration B - Alert noise and ownership clarity (5 weeks)
  - Compress: capture top 10 noisy alerts across inference-gateway. Hypothesis: routing error alerts lack context and are firing across teams.
  - Expand: change alert severity, attach runbook links, add contextual tags (model_id, route_id). Pilot with two product teams.
  - Contract: create alert ownership matrix, reduce paging alerts by 60% for non-critical signals, add automated suppression for known transient alerts.
3) Iteration C - Graceful fallback policy test (5 weeks)
  - Compress: design routing fallback to compatible smaller model when latency > SLO for > 500ms.
  - Expand: run canary route-level fallback with traffic shaping.
  - Contract: evaluate quality impact with sampled user prompts; if acceptable, add to routing policy library.

Roles & coordination (RACI-lite):
- Owners: platform-engineering (primary coordinators), serving-runtime (implementation), SRE (observability & alerts), product (impact sign-off), solutions-eng (customer-facing communication when Dedicated/private customers involved).
- Decision authority: platform-engineering lead for rollout gates under 10% traffic; product director + SRE director for >10% or cross-region rollouts.

Deliverables per iteration (minimum):
- SLO doc stub (1 page): SLO name, target, measurement window, owner, alert threshold.
- Runbook (short): quick triage, mitigation steps, postmortem triggers.
- Dashboard tiles: latency distribution, error-type breakdown, rollout % gauge.
- Automation tickets: alert suppression config, rollout orchestration change.

Instrumentation & metrics plan (practical):
- Use existing trace sampling (1%) plus targeted high-fidelity sampling for affected routes.
- Metric names and labels: keep canonical names (serving.latency_ms p99, serving.kv_cold_hit_ratio), ensure consistent labels: cluster, model_variant, route_id.
- Acceptance thresholds: show 95% CI for 72-hour windows before and after changes.

Communication cadence:
- Weekly 30-min sync across owners during Expand phase (calendar: #reliability-ops epic thread).
- Biweekly status snapshot for exec stakeholders (1 slide, 1 metric, 1 blocker).
- Post-iteration 15-min demo + 1-pager retrospective.

Gating criteria to move from Expand -> Contract:
- No more than 2 severity-P1 events in the 7-day expand window attributable to the experiment.
- Measured improvement on at least one leading metric (e.g., P99 down by >= 10%) OR reduction in alert volume >= 30%.
- Runbook draft exists and is reviewed by SRE.

Dependencies & quick wins:
- Dependency: KV-prefetch library work (infra ticket), requires small change in serving-runtime API (PR #87).
- Quick wins: small alert label additions and dashboard tiles we can ship in 2 days. Prioritize these in every Compress phase.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: experiments cause regressions in user-facing quality (model outputs). Mitigation: conservative fallback with quality sampling and human review on failures > threshold.
- Risk: coordination overhead grows with parallel threads. Mitigation: limit concurrent expansions to 3 and require registration in the iteration registry.

Success metrics (first 3 iterations):
- 20% reduction in noisy-page incidents for target services.
- P99 latency reduction >= 10% for at least one target route.
- 3 runbooks authored and onboarded into SRE runbook library.

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Maya: schedule kickoff for Iteration A compress (target Jan 18).
- Ethan: open instrumentation PR and add sampling probes (JIRA-REL-1501).
- Lina: prepare canary config and traffic shaping playbook.
- Arjun: confirm product acceptance criteria and customer impact matrix.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Which Dedicated customer clusters should be in the initial testbed? (Sofia to propose list)
- Can we get 24/7 alert coverage for Expand windows crossing weekends? (SRE ops rota ask)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep retros concise. One painful lesson: last year we waited too long to automate suppression and it cost 3 days of escalations. Avoid that.
notes: Working doc; expect to iterate. Register accordion threads in Confluence registry and tag all PRs with JIRA-REL tickets. Use #reliability-ops for daily chatter.
